title: The influence of reactivating imagery rehearsal therapy in individuals with frequent idiopathic nightmares on cortical hyperarousal
summary:
Imagery Rehearsal Therapy (IRT) is a well-known and effective treatment for nightmares in which patients develop a new, neutral or positive sequence to their original nightmare and then imagine this new dream sequence at night before going to bed. Although IRT has often been shown to be effective, it is still unclear exactly how it works and what changes occur in the brain.
New studies suggest that the effect of IRT can be enhanced if the new dream sequence (also known as imagination) is reactivated during sleep. This reactivation can occur, for example, through a scent that is released both during the imagination of the new dream sequence and during sleep. In this study, the effect of the reactivation of IRT on brain activity will be investigated.

interventions.name: Imagery Rehearsal Therapy WITH targeted memory reactivation with an odor during sleep
Imagery Rehearsal Therapy WITHOUT targeted memory reactivation with an odor during sleep

criteria:
Inclusion criteria:
At least one nightmare per week (nightmare defined as a vivid dream experience full of fear and anxiety, from which one usually wakes up with a fairly accurate memory)
Exclusion criteria:
current psychiatric or sleep disorders (except nightmares)
taking medication that affects sleep (e.g. hypnotics, antidepressants, anxiolytics, beta-blockers, benzodiazepines, stimulants)
IQ <80
systemic, neurological or brain diseases
insufficient communication skills in the German language
no shift work or intercontinental flights in the last 30 days 
allergies to fragrances used in the study
